purpose: S072 constrained Gaussian retarded boundary-transfer response and finite-time tracking bound

sources.reading_scope: Sections 4.1 and 4.2.2 read in full. Equations 55-56 constrain the exceptional vector mode; equation 74 at n=2,K=1 yields the electromagnetic dipole mass 2/r^2+4Q^2/r^4 for arbitrary cosmological constant. Used to check the constrained matter-free limit, after four-dimensional electromagnetic duality. The charged-fermion Gaussian response is derived separately.

Appendix A reread in full: positive Schwinger mass, bosonized gauge-current sector and angular representation. Adopt its positive physical polarization coefficient in our mostly-plus Lorentz convention. The coupled magnetic-AdS source projection comes from the preceding angular-boundary calculation; no nonlinear non-Abelian completion or physical switch is imported.

Sections IV, V.1 and VI read. The available v1's assignment of physical versus constraint modes after equations 26-27 conflicts with the constrained Kodama-Ishibashi equation and the neutral electromagnetic dipole limit. That assignment is not adopted; this source is retained as an inspected comparator, not affirmative verification. No broader correction or publication claim.

inherited_evidence.role: Static fixed-source coefficients and candidate family; neither was previously a finite-frequency transfer theorem.

novelty: Constrained RN modes, Schwinger polarization and spectral positivity are prior methods. The explicit causal comparison is an ordinary derivation; no exhaustive novelty acceptance.
limitations: The transfer port has prescribed bosonized matter phase and permits a boundary current
The actual two-sided fermion junction and prepared-state covariance/noise are not matched
The background is a fixed RN exterior, not the evolving opened wormhole
